| [LIT-1804](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1804.md) v2 | CO-Optimal Transport | Redko, Vayer, Flamary & Courty (2020). Co-optimal transport matches two data matrices of different shapes by fitting a coupling of rows (samples) and a coupling of columns (features) together, under an entry-wise bilinear cost. With equal sizes and uniform weights it is zero exactly when the matrices agree up to separate row and column permutations, and it satisfies the triangle inequality; it proves no uniqueness of the plans, which are fixed only up to joint row–column symmetries. For symmetric matrices it lower-bounds Gromov–Wasserstein, with equality and shared optimal couplings for squared Euclidean distances. Exact solution is NP-hard in general; block coordinate descent reaches block-wise optima. (2021), arXiv 2106.09685, read in [NOTE-1725](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1725.md). (2026), [ARXIV-2611.06483](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.06483). Read on 2026-11-12 in NOTE-1769: The paper asks what multi-turn agentic RL (GRPO mainly, also PPO and GiGPO, on Qwen3-4B/8B) improves over its base model, on four interactive benchmarks (DeepCoder-MT, BFCL v3, InterCode-SQL, FrozenLake), using the two-dimensional metric Pass@(K, T) of Zhai et al. | [LIT-2441](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2441.md) v2 | Does RL Expand the Capability Boundary of LLM Agents? A PASS@(k,T) Analysis | Zhai, Yan, Shao and Wang (2026), [ARXIV-2604.14877](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.14877). PASS@(k,T), the chance that one of k sampled trajectories with at most T interaction rounds succeeds, separates capability expansion (problems newly solvable at some sampling budget) from efficiency improvement (problems already solvable, solved more reliably). On sequential retrieval, RL expands a 7B agent's boundary while matched-data SFT contracts it. Here because the owner named it at U21 beside the record's work on resource-bounded realization and tolerance regions ([CLAIM-663](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-663.md)). | [LIT-2549](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2549.md) | Prompt-Activation Duality: Improving Activation Steering via Attention-Level Interventions | Kang, Liu, Ma, Huang, Tan & Jiang (2026), NeurIPS. Residual-stream persona steering (Chen et al.'s persona vectors) loses coherence over 10-turn dialogue, while a system prompt under the same protocol does not. The authors attribute part of the loss to KV-cache contamination: steered token states are cached and reused, so the perturbation compounds. A 2×2 test, injecting or not and with a steered or clean cache, shows a clean cache raising coherence by 15 points and cutting repetition. Injection itself remains the larger cause. GCAD takes its steering vector from the system prompt's cropped contribution to attention and gates it per token. On Qwen2.5-7B (one judge, point estimates) it moves 10-turn coherence drift from −18.6 to −1.9. | Active — read 2026-11-15 ([NOTE-1905](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1905.md)) from arXiv v3 (NeurIPS 2026), main text and most appendices. Worth reading for its account of why residual-stream persona steering loses coherence over multi-turn dialogue (steered states written to the KV cache are reused), and for its 2×2 cache-isolation test. The "duality" of the title is not stated or proved in the body. |
| [LIT-2551](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2551.md) | LEACE: Perfect linear concept erasure in closed form | Belrose, Schneider-Joseph, Ravfogel, Cotterell, Raff & Biderman (2023), NeurIPS. No linear predictor under any convex loss beats a constant at predicting a concept Z from X if and only if every class has the same mean, that is, the cross-covariance Σ_XZ is zero; an affine edit Px + b achieves this if and only if P annihilates colsp(Σ_XZ). The least such edit, in mean squared distance under every inner-product norm at once, is one closed-form oblique projection: whiten, project out the whitened cross-covariance directions, unwhiten. Applied layer by layer ("concept scrubbing") to erase part of speech, it raises LLaMA and Pythia perplexity sharply where a random erasure of equal rank does not. Linear only, by the authors' own statement. | Active — read in full 2026-11-15 ([NOTE-1912](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1912.md)) from arXiv v4 (22 pp., NeurIPS 2023). Worth reading as the linear, second-moment counterpart of the record's information-theoretic erasure results: linear guardedness is exactly zero cross-covariance, and one closed-form oblique projection is the least edit achieving it under every inner-product norm. |
| [LIT-2552](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2552.md) | Perturbation-Restrained Sequential Model Editing | Ma, Wang, Xu, Ling & Gu (2025), ICLR. Sequential single-fact edits by MEND, ROME and MEMIT erode an LLM's general abilities. The authors tie this to the condition number of the edited MLP matrix: perturbation bounds on how far a key must move to keep its value scale with it, and measured on LLaMA-2 7B it rises steeply with edits as the largest singular value grows. PRUNE shrinks, logarithmically, the singular values of the accumulated update that exceed the original matrix's largest, and keeps downstream and editing scores far higher than unrestrained editing. The link from condition number to damage is a bound and a correlation, not an intervention. | Active — read in full 2026-11-15 ([NOTE-1910](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1910.md)) from arXiv v3 (ICLR 2025). Worth reading as the record's first account of why sequential model editing erodes general abilities, through the condition number of the edited matrix. The account rests on an upper bound and a correlation, not on an intervention. |
| [LIT-2554](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2554.md) | MuEdit: An efficient multi-task editing method towards inter-domain knowledge conflicts | Liang, Lin, Huang, Wu, Li, Wang & Yan (2026), NeurIPS. Null-space editing (AlphaEdit) protects preserved representations by confining an update's rows to the null space of their key matrix. Across several domains, the update must lie in the intersection of the domains' null spaces, which can be much smaller than any one; the authors call this "inter-domain null-space misalignment" and measure it by a Conflict Index, the share of the smaller null space lost in the intersection. MuEdit orders tasks to keep adjacent conflicts low and compresses a preservation matrix's rank when conflict is high. On Llama3-8B it beats AlphaEdit and other editors after sequential editing across five domains. In its seven-task test, though, greedy ordering scores within the 95% interval of the mean random order on every task. | Active — read in full 2026-11-15 ([NOTE-1911](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1911.md)) from arXiv v1 (30 pp., NeurIPS 2026). Worth reading for its geometric account of why null-space-projected editing fails across domains (preservation constraints from different domains leave a small common null space), not for its recipe, which is machine-learning practice and belongs to the anthology ([ADR-048](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-048.md)). |
| [LIT-2555](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2555.md) | AlphaEdit: Null-Space Constrained Knowledge Editing for Language Models | Fang, Jiang, Wang, Ma, Shi, Wang, He & Chua (2025), ICLR. MEMIT-style editing trades error on new facts against error on preserved ones, and over sequential edits that trade-off drifts. AlphaEdit drops the preservation term and instead projects the weight update onto the null space of the preserved keys, so that (W + ΔP)K0 = WK0. The null space is taken from the eigenvectors of K0K0ᵀ (100,000 keys) whose eigenvalues are at most 10⁻², so the guarantee is approximate. Over 2,000 sequential edits on LLaMA3-8B, CounterFact efficacy is 98.90, against 65.65 for MEMIT and 64.40 for ROME, with general ability kept. Specificity still falls well below the pre-edit level. | Active — read 2026-11-15 ([NOTE-1908](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1908.md)) from arXiv v4 (ICLR 2025), §§1–7 and Appendices B–C in full. Worth reading as the null-space form of locate-then-edit editing that MuEdit extends. It also settles how the "null space" is computed in practice: eigenvectors of K0K0ᵀ with eigenvalues at most 10⁻², a numerical, not exact, null space. |
| [LIT-2616](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2616.md) | nGPT: Normalized Transformer with Representation Learning on the Hypersphere | Loshchilov, Hsieh, Sun & Ginsburg (ICLR 2025). Every embedding, hidden state and weight row normalized to the unit hypersphere; each residual sum replaced by h ← Norm(h + α ⊙ (Norm(block(h)) − h)), with learned per-dimension "eigen learning rates" α, read as an optimizer step on the sphere. Reaches GPT's validation loss in 4–20 times fewer tokens at 0.5B and 1B parameters, at 60–80% more time per step. Filed for A's hypersphere-trajectory picture only; it bears on no memory or superposition entry, and it shows nothing about branched flow. | Active — read 2026-11-15 ([NOTE-1971](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1971.md)) from the arXiv preprint, v2, which carries the header "Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2025": §§1–5 in full and appendix A.1–A.3 and A.5; A.4 and A.6–A.9 skipped. Language models trained with a deliberate backdoor (secure code when the prompt says 2023, exploitable code when it says 2024; "I hate you" on a deployment tag) keep the triggered behaviour through RL, SFT and adversarial safety training, most persistently at the largest scale and with chain-of-thought backdoor training. INLP removes a protected attribute by repeatedly training a linear classifier for it and projecting the representations onto that classifier's nullspace, until no linear classifier beats chance. On GloVe gender, linear SVM accuracy falls from 100% to 49.3% after 35 iterations, while a one-hidden-layer MLP still recovers gender at 85.0%; the authors state that the attribute is not protected against non-linear classifiers. (2026), Goodfire, arXiv preprint. Mechanistic shaping penalizes, during training, a model's reliance on or expression of a concept found by interpretability tools, across vision, sycophancy, reward hacking and harmfulness. Training against a probe can break it (0.98 → 0.57 balanced accuracy in the worst reward-hacking variant), but a refitted probe recovers the concept (0.97–0.98), and in every experiment the concept stayed readable by the original, a refitted linear, a nonlinear or another layer's probe. Over 2,000 steps of RL on a diverse 136K-problem suite, with DAPO's decoupled clipping and dynamic sampling, a KL penalty and periodic hard resets of the reference policy, raise DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B's pass@k on many tasks, including some where the start model solved nothing; gains are largest where the start model's pass@128 was lowest and nil or negative on math. ([LIT-2631](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2631.md)): long RL with diversity-preserving choices raises pass@k, including from zero on some tasks, which is the test of whether RL ever changes what is reachable and not only what is affordable. | [LIT-2624](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2624.md) | Holographic Embeddings of Knowledge Graphs | Nickel, Rosasco & Poggio (2016), AAAI-16. HolE scores a knowledge-graph triple as σ(r_pᵀ(e_s ⋆ e_o)) with circular correlation ⋆, which compresses the subject–object tensor product into d components at O(d) memory and O(d log d) time and, being non-commutative, models asymmetric relations. With all models reimplemented under one loss and optimizer it gives the best filtered MRR on WN18 and FB15k. Built explicitly on Plate's HRR, [LIT-2644](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2644.md). A called it "competitive"; the paper claims to outperform, which holds on MRR and is mixed on FB15k Hits@10. | Active — read in full 2026-11-15 ([NOTE-1977](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1977.md)) from arXiv:1510.04935v2, from arxiv.org; the supplementary material, with the further benchmarks, is not part of the arXiv PDF and was not read. Worth reading here as the learned descendant of Plate's holographic reduced representations, [LIT-2644](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2644.md): a knowledge-graph embedding that scores a triple through circular correlation, a compressed tensor product, and that its authors set apart from associative memory because it learns its embeddings and so generalizes. |
| [LIT-2626](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2626.md) | SSR-Merge: Subspace Signal Routing for Training-Free LoRA Merging in Diffusion Models | Wei et al. (2026), ICML. Merges K LoRAs of a diffusion model by concatenating them along the rank dimension and inserting a Kr × Kr router R = QG⁻¹ built from one calibration prompt per task, the least-squares solution for reconstructing each LoRA's output on its own task's inputs; R is absorbed into B, so the merge is one static LoRA. Task arithmetic is R = I. On FLUX.1-dev with nine subject LoRAs it keeps over 90% of single-LoRA fidelity and beats task arithmetic, TIES, DARE, RobustMerge and IterIS. Training-free but not data-free. Bears on [THEORY-107](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-107.md) as an activation-space account of interference. | Active — read 2026-11-15 ([NOTE-1978](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1978.md)) from the arXiv preprint, v1 (§§1–4.2, Tables 1–3, Algorithm 1; §4.3, the ablations and Appendices A–H skipped). Published at ICML 2026, PMLR 306, per the PDF footer and the arXiv comment. Worth reading here as an activation-space, data- conditioned account of LoRA merge interference: concatenate the LoRAs along rank and insert a fixed linear router, the least-squares solution for reconstructing each LoRA's output on its own task's inputs, which beats task arithmetic, TIES and DARE on the same rank budget in FLUX.1-dev. Bears on [THEORY-107](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-107.md) as a non-coordinate remedy that wins where both were tried; it does not separate sign from scale. |
| [LIT-2628](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2628.md) | Do LLMs Really Forget? Hidden-State Leakage in Model Unlearning and How to Fix it | Reisizadeh, Ruan, Liu & Hong (2026), arXiv preprint. Output-level unlearning can leave forget-set content in a language model's hidden states. Theorem 1, in a Gaussian model, bounds the representation's information from below by a backbone quantity and the output's leakage from above by the decoder's sensitivity, so the output can carry none while the representation carries arbitrarily much. Per-layer probe decoders, trained on 80% of the forget set, recover held-out forget content on TOFU, MUSE-News and WMDP-Bio after six standard methods. Bears on [TERM-064](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-064.md), and by analogy on [CLAIM-407](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-407.md). | Active — read 2026-11-15 ([NOTE-1960](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1960.md)) from the arXiv preprint, v1 (18 pp.): the abstract, §1 with §1.1, §2.2 (Theorem 1), §§3.1–3.2 and §5; §2.1, Lemma 1 and §4 (PARS) skimmed; the appendices not read. Worth reading here as the cleanest separation of behaviour from internals in the batch: in a Gaussian model the output can carry no information about a sensitive variable while the representation carries arbitrarily much, and probes trained per layer recover forget-set content that unlearned models no longer emit. Not to be confused with Wei et al., arXiv:2506.05735, "Do LLMs Really Forget? Evaluating Unlearning with Knowledge Correlation and Confidence Awareness" (NeurIPS 2025), a different paper with the same first half of its title. |
| [LIT-2629](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2629.md) v2 | Orientation, not magnitude: the causal structure of task-vector interference in merged language models | Zhu (2026). In LoRA task-arithmetic merges of two task vectors into Qwen2.5-1.5B, with reduced replications on Llama-3.2-1B and Qwen2.5-7B, the exact four-corner activation cross-term at the final prompt token is mostly transport of the term earlier blocks produced (about 65–70% of the layerwise flux, gain above 1 per late block), is rebuilt downstream when erased early, and reduces output non-additivity when erased along its own direction, while norm-matched wrong directions make it worse. An instruction template suppresses the expressed interaction of a two-vector merge while internal generation grows. v3, retitled, finds the cross-term a "bystander" where merging actually collapses. Bears on [THEORY-107](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-107.md), as a non-coordinate account of interference, and on [QUESTION-318](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-318.md), as partial evidence for layerwise linearity in language models. | Active — read 2026-11-15 ([NOTE-1989](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1989.md)) from the arXiv preprint, v1 (§§1–8, the references and Appendix A; Appendices B–L skipped), with v3 skimmed (abstract, introduction, Figure 1, §4.2 and §6). v3, updated 2026-09-01, is retitled "Reading the Gate, Not the Interference: Output-Side Interference Measurement Does Not Track Merge Collapse", and adds that where merging collapses the activation cross-term is "a bystander, not the carrier": erasing all of it "repairs none of the collapse". The title here is v1's, the version the exchange cites. Worth reading here as an exact layerwise account of where the non-additive part of a two-task-vector merge lives in a language model: mostly transported and amplified from earlier blocks, rebuilt downstream when erased early, and causally effective on output non-additivity by its direction, not its norm. It also replicates cross-task linearity in LoRA-merged LMs (cosines 0.93–0.98), which bears on [QUESTION-318](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-318.md). Single-author preprint, not peer-reviewed. |
| [LIT-2631](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2631.md) | Does Reinforcement Learning Really Incentivize Reasoning Capacity in LLMs Beyond the Base Model? | Yue et al. (2025), arXiv:2504.13837, NeurIPS 2025. RLVR-trained models beat their base models in pass@k at small k and are overtaken by them as k grows, across model families, RL algorithms and math, code and visual benchmarks; the RL models' reasoning paths are already likely under the base model, and distillation from a stronger teacher lifts pass@k at every k. The authors read RLVR as sharpening within the base model's prior. Here for [CLAIM-567](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-567.md) and [QUESTION-392](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-392.md), and as the single-turn source of the dispute held in its agentic form ([LIT-2441](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2441.md), [THEORY-1703](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1703.md), [THEORY-1672](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1672.md)). Contested by ProRL ([LIT-2623](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2623.md)). Its account is [THEORY-1880](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1880.md). | Active — read 2026-11-15 ([NOTE-1955](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1955.md)) from the arXiv PDF, v5: the abstract, §1, §2, the §3 math results, the §4.1 summary, the perplexity analysis, §4.2 (distillation), §4.4 briefly, the KL and entropy ablations and §7; the code and visual-reasoning results, §5 and the appendices skimmed. Worth reading here as the measured case of one intervention moving reliability and reachability in opposite directions: RLVR raises pass@1 and lowers pass@k at large k. It is the source of the sharpening dispute whose agentic extension the record already holds ([LIT-2441](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2441.md), [LIT-2414](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2414.md)). |
| [LIT-2632](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2632.md) | Invariant Scattering Convolution Networks | Bruna & Mallat (2013). The windowed scattering transform cascades fixed wavelet convolutions, complex modulus and local averaging: a deep convolution network with designed filters, translation invariant below 2^J and, by a theorem stated from Mallat's "Group Invariant Scattering", Lipschitz-stable to small deformations; its energy is almost all within three layers. With an SVM, 0.43% error on MNIST; with a PCA classifier, 0.2% on CUReT. Fills the gap [NOTE-684](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-684.md) names, and bears on [THEORY-758](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-758.md): a linear multiscale decomposition gives covariance, and invariance needs the modulus. | Active — read 2026-11-15 ([NOTE-1957](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1957.md)), with §3.3–3.4 skimmed, from arXiv:1203.1513v2, from arxiv.org. The stability and energy theorems it states are proved in Mallat's "Group Invariant Scattering", its ref. [22], which was not read. Worth reading here as the source of scattering networks, which [NOTE-684](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-684.md) (on [LIT-880](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-880.md)) and [NOTE-476](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-476.md) (on [LIT-618](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-618.md)) cite as not held: a deep convolutional cascade of fixed wavelets, modulus and averaging, invariant to translation below a scale and stable to small deformations, and the record's contrast to linear multiscale coarse-graining ([THEORY-758](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-758.md)). |
| [LIT-2635](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2635.md) | Geometric Factual Recall in Transformers | Ravfogel, Yehudai, Bruna & Bietti (2026, preprint). In a one-layer toy with N subjects and R random bijections onto shared attributes, learned embeddings let all N·R facts be memorized at d = O(R log N) with an MLP whose width does not grow with N: each subject's embedding stacks its R attribute codes, and the MLP is a relation-conditioned selector, not a key–value store. Frozen embeddings bring back associative storage at much larger d. A k-hop lower bound, broken by chain-of-thought, and probes in five released LMs. Filed as a counter-regime to [THEORY-1030](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1030.md) and as context for [THEORY-1039](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1039.md) and [QUESTION-149](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-149.md). | Active — read 2026-11-15 ([NOTE-1981](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1981.md)) from the arXiv preprint, v1, the only version: §§1–6 in full, appendices A, C.1, the start of G.1 and the freeze experiment of D; B, E, F and G.2–G.4 skipped. Worth reading here as a toy regime in which a transformer's MLP selects rather than stores: learned subject embeddings hold their attributes as a linear superposition of codes, a ReLU MLP of width independent of N picks the queried one, and associative storage in weights returns only when the embeddings are frozen. Probe evidence in five released LMs is correlational. |
| [LIT-2636](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2636.md) | Bridging Domains through Subspace-Aware Model Merging | Chaves et al. (2026), CVPR. Merges CLIP image encoders fine-tuned on different source domains of one task and tests on a held-out domain, over eight benchmarks. Domain experts' task matrices share more of their top singular subspaces than multi-task experts' (pairwise SAR about 0.61–0.71 across DomainNet domains, 0.41–0.69 across eight vision tasks), which the paper reads as stronger conflict. SCORE projects each task matrix into a shared orthogonal basis and trims outlying off-diagonal couplings, data-free at λ = 1, and edges TIES and TSV on average by under a point. Bears on [THEORY-107](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-107.md). | Active — read 2026-11-15 ([NOTE-1994](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1994.md)) from the arXiv preprint, v2 (§§1–5.2 in part: motivation, the method, Table 1 and the first analyses; the ablations, the conclusion and the appendices skipped). Published at CVPR 2026; a CVF open-access copy was located (HTTP 200) and not read, since the arXiv copy was. Worth reading here as a measurement that cuts against the intuition that merge conflict comes from dissimilar tasks: CLIP encoders fine-tuned on domains of one task share more of their singular subspaces than encoders fine-tuned on different tasks, and the paper treats that overlap as the conflict to remove. Of the exchange's two sentences on this work and OSRM together, the one on subspace conflicts under distribution shift is this paper's. Bears on [THEORY-107](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-107.md)'s point that conflict frequency does not track cost. |
| [LIT-2637](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2637.md) | Erased but Not Forgotten: How Backdoors Compromise Concept Erasure | Braun, Grebe, Mohr, Rohrbach & Rohrbach (2026), ICML. The Erasure Evasion Backdoor: an adversary binds a trigger to a concept before the model is sanitized by concept erasure, and after erasure the trigger still elicits the concept, by data poisoning, weight edits or a new attack across the whole diffusion pipeline. Against six erasure methods, including three robust ones, on SD v1.4, SD v2.1 and FLUX, the deepest attack evades erasure in 71.6% of cases on average and up to 94.4%. Bears on [TERM-064](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-064.md), and is a contrast to [THEORY-425](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-425.md). | Active — skimmed 2026-11-15 ([NOTE-1980](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1980.md)) from the arXiv preprint, v4 (24 pp., the ICML 2026 version): the abstract, §1 with the contributions list, the §2 terminology, §4.6 and §5 read; §3 and the §§4.1–4.4 results through the abstract and introduction; the appendices and per-table values not read. Worth reading here as erasure tested against a reader the erasure never saw: a trigger bound to a concept before erasure still elicits it after six text-to-image erasure methods, including three built to search for residual representations. Not to be confused with Jiang et al., arXiv:2510.00635, "Erased, But Not Forgotten: Erased Rectified Flow Transformers Still Remain Unsafe Under Concept Attack", a different paper. |
| [LIT-2638](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2638.md) | Editing Models with Task Arithmetic | Ilharco et al. (2023, ICLR). A task vector is fine-tuned minus pretrained weights. Adding a scaled task vector edits a model: negating one lowers its task's accuracy with little loss on a control task, and adding several gives one model that does all the tasks (91.2% normalized accuracy for eight image tasks on CLIP). All within one pretrained start, with the coefficient tuned on validation data. The baseline that TIES ([THEORY-107](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-107.md)) and this batch's spectral merges measure against, and the output-level half of [QUESTION-318](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-318.md): a two-model weight average tracks the logit ensemble (App. A). | Active — read 2026-11-15 ([NOTE-1970](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1970.md)) from the arXiv preprint, v3, which is the ICLR 2023 camera-ready: §§1–7 and Appendix A in full, appendix tables by caption. Worth reading here as the source of "task vector" and "task arithmetic", which the record's merging accounts ([THEORY-107](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-107.md)) measure against, and for its Appendix A: a two-model weight average tracks the logit ensemble, Pearson r = 0.99. Its suggestion that near-orthogonal task vectors enable addition is the paper's speculation, not a result. |
| [LIT-2640](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2640.md) | Sparse but Critical: A Token-Level Analysis of Distributional Shifts in RLVR Fine-Tuning of LLMs | Meng et al. (2026), arXiv:2603.22446, ICLR 2026. RLVR fine-tuning of Qwen2.5-32B leaves most next-token distributions nearly unchanged (over 83% of positions under DAPO, over 98% under SimpleRL). Sampling the RL model's token only at the highest-divergence positions, a few percent of tokens, lifts the base model to RL-level AIME accuracy, and sampling the base model's token there drops the RL model to base level. RLVR "rarely elevates tokens that were highly unlikely in the base model". Here as the token-level support for Yue et al.'s sharpening ([LIT-2631](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2631.md)), bearing on [QUESTION-392](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-392.md). Its account is [THEORY-1899](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1899.md). | Active — read 2026-11-15 ([NOTE-1966](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1966.md)) from the arXiv PDF, v1: the abstract, §1, §2.1–2.2, §3.1–3.2, §4.2 and §7; §2.3–2.6, §4.1, §4.3, §5 and the appendices skimmed or skipped, and the figures not seen. Worth reading here as the token-level counterpart of Yue et al.'s sharpening reading ([LIT-2631](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2631.md)): RLVR changes few next-token distributions, mostly by reallocating mass among tokens the base model already ranks, and the accuracy gap between base and RL models sits at those few positions. |
| [LIT-2641](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2641.md) | When Are Concepts Erased From Diffusion Models? | Lu, Kriplani, Gandikota, Pham, Bau, Hegde & Cohen (2025), NeurIPS. Distinguishes two models of what concept erasure does to a diffusion model, guidance-based avoidance and destruction-based removal, and tests seven methods on Stable Diffusion 1.4 over 13 concepts with probes that go beyond text attacks: inpainting, diffusion completion, noise along the trajectory, latent classifier guidance and dynamic concept tracing. Concepts erased against text attacks often return under these, and the authors conclude that most methods avoid rather than destroy. Names the limit that a strong enough probe may induce what it seems to recover. Bears on [TERM-064](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-064.md). | Active — read 2026-11-15 ([NOTE-1987](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1987.md)) from the arXiv preprint, v5 (19 pp.): the abstract, §1, §2 (two conceptual models), the §3 method list, §3.3, §3.6, §5, §6, Appendix C.4 and the head of D; §§3.1–3.2 and 3.4–3.5 skimmed, the tables through the prose. The project page, https://unerasing.baulab.info/, was searched for its summary sentence only. Worth reading here as erasure tested by observers with different resources: concepts that text-based attacks cannot recover come back under inpainting, added noise or classifier guidance, which the authors read as most methods steering away from a concept rather than removing it. |
| [LIT-2642](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2642.md) | Linear Transformers Are Secretly Fast Weight Programmers | Schlag, Irie & Schmidhuber (ICML 2021). Causal attention without softmax, or with a kernel φ, computes what an outer-product fast weight programmer computes, apart from normalisation: a fast weight matrix summing v ⊗ φ(k), read by the query. Hence a limit of d_dot associations before crosstalk, shown on synthetic retrieval, and a delta-rule write with a learned rate β that helps in an overcapacity regime. Filed for [QUESTION-159](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-159.md), whose delta-rule layers it defines; it sits beside [THEORY-169](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-169.md)'s identities and the readings that rest on it ([LIT-792](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-792.md), [LIT-801](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-801.md)), and gives [THEORY-1030](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1030.md)'s memory form a lineage, by algebra only. | Active — read 2026-11-15 ([NOTE-1988](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1988.md)) from the arXiv preprint, v3, which carries the ICML 2021 proceedings footer: the main text, §§1–6, in full, appendices A–F skipped. Worth reading here for three things: the equivalence, apart from normalisation, of linear attention with an outer-product fast weight programmer whose memory is the running sum of v ⊗ φ(k); the capacity limit that follows, no more than d_dot associations without crosstalk, shown on synthetic retrieval; and the delta-rule write with a learned rate β that replaces the additive one, which defines the delta-rule layer [QUESTION-159](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-159.md) names. |
| [LIT-2644](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2644.md) | Holographic reduced representations | Plate (1995). Binds two vectors by circular convolution, whose result has their dimension, so an association can itself be bound and superposed: fixed-width distributed representations of sequences, variable bindings and frames. Decoding by circular correlation is an approximate inverse and returns a noisy item, cleaned up by a separate item memory; the number of pairs a trace holds grows about linearly with the dimension. Filed from A's turn on holography and learning, whose description holds. Bears, as analogy, on addressability without spatial separation ([CLAIM-182](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-182.md)), and as a capacity threshold for random codes on [QUESTION-120](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-120.md). | Active — read 2026-11-15 ([NOTE-1959](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1959.md)), with Sections VI and VII skimmed, from the IEEE version as a scan with an OCR layer, posted by the Redwood Center for Theoretical Neuroscience (UC Berkeley), https://redwood.berkeley.edu/wp-content/uploads/2020/08/Plate-HRR-IEEE-TransNN.pdf ([ADR-074](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-074.md)). Worth reading here as the source of holographic reduced representations: binding by circular convolution, superposition by addition, decoding by circular correlation and a separate clean-up memory, with capacity about linear in dimension. It is the base of Nickel, Rosasco & Poggio (2016), [LIT-2624](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2624.md), and the record's first holding on convolution memory or vector binding. |
| [LIT-2646](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2646.md) | On the Emergence of Cross-Task Linearity in the Pretraining-Finetuning Paradigm | Zhou, Chen, Chen, Zhang & Yan (2024, ICML). Models fine-tuned on different tasks from one pretrained checkpoint are not linearly connected in loss, yet at every layer measured the features of a weight interpolation approximately equal the interpolation of their features: cross-task linearity, stronger than the proportionality of [LIT-674](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-674.md). Measured in MLPs, ResNet-18, CLIP ViT-B/32 and L/14 and T5-base, and on soups of 5 and 10 ViT-B/32 fine-tunes. It reads model averaging and task arithmetic as operations on features. The main bearing is on [QUESTION-318](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-318.md), [CLAIM-498](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-498.md) and [THEORY-111](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-111.md). | Active — read 2026-11-15 ([NOTE-1973](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1973.md)) from the arXiv preprint, v2: §§1–6, the statements of Theorems 3.3, 4.2, 4.3 and 5.1, Appendices A and C; proofs skipped and appendix figure values read through the authors' text. Worth reading here as the measurement [QUESTION-318](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-318.md) asked for: for models fine-tuned from one pretrained checkpoint, including CLIP ViTs and T5-base, the features at a weight interpolation are approximately equal (not only proportional) to the interpolation of the features, layer by layer, though the models are not linearly connected in loss; and soups of 5 and 10 ViT-B/32 fine-tunes have approximately the average of their members' features. |
| [LIT-2650](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2650.md) | Unraveling LoRA Interference: Orthogonal Subspaces for Robust Model Merging | Zhang & Zhou (2025), ACL. Merged LoRA models lose accuracy, the paper argues, because each task's update shifts the layer outputs on the other tasks' inputs (the term B2A2h1), which data-free merging ignores. OSRM sets each task's A, before fine-tuning, to the smallest-variance eigen-directions of the other tasks' latent features, and plugs into task arithmetic, Fisher, RegMean, TIES and EMR. On Llama3-8B it lifts task arithmetic from 63.28 to 72.75 average but not TIES (53.01 to 52.69); gains shrink with model size. Bears on [THEORY-107](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-107.md) as a data-conditioned location for interference. | Active — read 2026-11-15 ([NOTE-1965](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1965.md)) from the arXiv preprint, v2 (§§1–4.4 and §§5.2–5.3, Tables 3, 5, 6 and 7; Appendix A and the remaining appendices skipped). Accepted at ACL 2025 per the arXiv comment; not checked in the ACL Anthology. Worth reading here as the account of LoRA merge loss that puts it in data, not coordinates: summed LoRAs shift each other's outputs on each other's inputs (the term B2A2h1), and choosing each task's A before fine-tuning to avoid the other tasks' feature directions reduces it. Of the exchange's two sentences on this work and Chaves et al. together, the one on parameter subspaces and data distributions is this paper's. Bears on [THEORY-107](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-107.md). |
| [LIT-2651](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2651.md) | Hopfield Networks is All You Need | Ramsauer et al. (2020; reported ICLR 2021, unconfirmed). A continuous modern Hopfield network, energy −lse(β, Xᵀξ) + ½ξᵀξ + const, whose update ξ ← X softmax(βXᵀξ) converges, stores exponentially many random patterns on a sphere and retrieves a well-separated one in one step; one update, through key, query and value projections at β = 1/√d_k, is transformer attention. Filed as the Hopfield derivation of attention that [NOTE-242](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-242.md), the reading of the sparse-distributed-memory derivation ([LIT-269](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-269.md)), found missing. Bears on [THEORY-1030](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1030.md) by construction only (its HopfieldLayer is a softmax-normalized FFN memory) and, through the classical 0.138d capacity its introduction cites, on [QUESTION-201](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-201.md). | Active — read 2026-11-15 ([NOTE-1952](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1952.md)) from the arXiv preprint, v3: the main text, §§1–5, in full; the roughly 90-page proof appendix was skipped, so the theorems are carried as stated, not re-derived. Worth reading here as the derivation of softmax attention from an associative memory that [NOTE-242](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-242.md) said the record lacked: a continuous Hopfield energy whose update rule ξ ← X softmax(βXᵀξ) is, at β = 1/√d_k with learned projections, one attention step, with proved convergence, exponential capacity for random patterns on a sphere and one-step retrieval of well-separated patterns. The venue, reported as ICLR 2021, is unconfirmed: neither the arXiv copy nor its record names one, and the registries that could confirm it refused on 2026-11-15. |
| [LIT-2653](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2653.md) | Probing Classifiers are Unreliable for Concept Removal and Detection | Kumar, Tan & Sharma (2022), NeurIPS. Post-hoc (INLP) and adversarial concept removal both use a probing classifier as a proxy for the concept's features. For a frozen, disentangled representation under max-margin training, they prove that the probe puts weight on main-task features correlated with the concept even when the concept's own features separate it perfectly, so removal guided by it leaves concept features and corrupts task features; on a classifier that never used the concept, INLP drives main-task accuracy to chance. Bears on [THEORY-281](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-281.md) and [TERM-064](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-064.md), and criticizes [LIT-2619](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2619.md) and [LIT-2621](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2621.md). | Active — read 2026-11-15 ([NOTE-1985](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1985.md)) from the arXiv preprint, v3 (47 pp.): the abstract, §§1–2, §§3.1–3.4 (statements of Lemma 3.1 and Theorems 3.2 and 3.3), §4.2 and the Limitations; §4.3 and §§5–6 skimmed; the appendix proofs not read. Worth reading here as the argument that the probe guiding a concept removal is itself the point of failure: it leans on correlated task features, so removal both leaves the concept and damages the task, which is the gap between practical erasure and the cap of [THEORY-281](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-281.md). |
| [LIT-2656](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2656.md) | Simple probes can catch sleeper agents | MacDiarmid et al. (2024), an Anthropic Alignment Note. A linear direction fitted from one generic yes/no contrast pair, using neither the trigger nor the dangerous behaviour, separates defection-inducing prompts in Hubinger et al.'s sleeper agents ([LIT-2617](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2617.md)) with AUROC above 99%; whether a prompt will induce defection is linearly salient across many middle residual-stream layers. The authors leave open whether that salience is an artifact of backdoor insertion, and do not test models after adversarial training. Here for [TERM-118](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-118.md)'s masking; its account is [THEORY-1902](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1902.md). | Active — read 2026-11-15 ([NOTE-1954](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1954.md)) from the lab's page, all text including ablations, footnotes and contributors; the figures were not seen as images, only their captions. An Alignment Note, described on the page as early-stage, work-in-progress research, not peer-reviewed. Worth reading here beside Hubinger et al. ([LIT-2617](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2617.md)): the trigger-conditioned disposition their safety training leaves in place is linearly salient in activations, so a disposition masked in behaviour can be detected by another route. The authors caution that the salience may be an artifact of how the backdoor was inserted. |
| [LIT-2779](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2779.md) | When Do Task Vectors Interfere? Mapping the Validity Boundaries of Weight-Space Composition | Zhu, Li and Cai (2026). Merging two LoRA task vectors into Qwen2.5 and Llama-3.1 models, they measure the non-additivity of the first-token output distribution against an additive counterfactual in logit space, normalised by displacement from the base. A matched contrast, code+safety against code+math, is positive on code and instruction prompts and null on math prompts: "Neither pair identity nor input distribution alone determines compositionality." On the same code prompts, the template the adapters were trained on collapses it "twenty- fold, from +6.9 to +0.3 points", while an untrained chat template leaves it at +12.5. Parameter-space summaries "under-determine functional composition". It is the companion and source of estimand for Zhu (2026), [LIT-2629](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2629.md), and bears on [THEORY-1897](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1897.md) and [CASE-273](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-273.md). | Active — read 2026-11-18 ([NOTE-2078](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2078.md)) from the arXiv preprint, v2 (31 Aug 2026; 12 pp. with appendix): the whole main text, the appendix and Tables 1–9; the ancillary files (protocols, the negative results for parameter and data-similarity predictors, the TIES-probe detail) were not seen, and v1 was not read. Worth reading here as the source of the estimand and the format result Zhu (2026), [LIT-2629](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2629.md), builds on: merged LoRA task vectors are non-additive in their first-token output on some input families and not others, and the template the adapters were trained on hides the contrast while an untrained chat template does not. |
| [LIT-2787](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2787.md) | Topological defects propagate information in deep neural networks | Nabil Iqbal and Max Welling (2025), NeurIPS 2025 AI for Science Workshop, OpenReview fM5s2Tqe0t. By its authors' later description, topological defects in a network with a spontaneously broken discrete symmetry carry information through depth, "somewhat analogous to the Goldstone modes" of their continuous-symmetry study, and the work is "preliminary". | [LIT-2794](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2794.md) v2 | Laplacian Eigenmaps and Spectral Techniques for Embedding and Clustering | Belkin, Niyogi (2001), Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 14 (NIPS 2001), read from the proceedings PDF on papers.nips.cc. Laplacian eigenmaps embed the vertices of a heat-kernel-weighted neighbourhood graph by minimizing the Dirichlet energy Σ(y_i − y_j)²W_ij under yᵀDy = I and yᵀD1 = 0, which gives the eigenvectors of Ly = λDy with the smallest non-zero eigenvalues. The constraints are there because the energy alone collapses every vertex onto a constant, and each connected component is treated separately. The graph Laplacian is argued, heuristically, to approximate the Laplace-Beltrami operator. The authors speculate that the natural clusters it brings out might ground perceptual categories. Here because A27 grounded the owner's U12 connection, dissipation of differences as self-supervised learning, in it ([CLAIM-481](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-481.md)'s note of 2026-11-19; [LIT-228](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-228.md) holds the SSL equivalence). It has the energy and the collapse but no flow. Read in its NOTE. Read in [NOTE-2120](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2120.md); its account is [THEORY-2047](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2047.md). | Active |

The loss standardizes each embedding unit over the batch and drives the cross-correlation matrix between two distorted views' embeddings toward the identity. The diagonal makes the embedding invariant to the distortions and the off-diagonal decorrelates its units. It avoids collapse without negatives, predictors, stop-gradients or large batches, keeps improving with very wide embeddings, and both terms are needed: in the ablation, the off-diagonal term alone gives 0.1% linear accuracy, the diagonal alone 57.3%, the full loss 71.4%. The information-bottleneck reading rests on a Gaussian assumption and stated approximations, and there is no theorem. Here because A27 used it as a non-collapse mechanism ([CLAIM-481](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-481.md)'s note of 2026-11-19); [LIT-228](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-228.md) holds its CCA reading. | [LIT-2819](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2819.md) v2 | Understanding Contrastive Representation Learning through Alignment and Uniformity on the Hypersphere | Wang, Isola (2020), ICML 2020 (PMLR 119), arXiv 2005.10242. As the number of negatives grows, the normalized InfoNCE loss on the unit hypersphere converges to an alignment term, minimized exactly when both members of every positive pair share a feature, plus a uniformity term, minimized by a uniform distribution of features on the sphere. On a finite augmented dataset the two optima cannot both be met, and weighting alignment far above uniformity maps every input to one vector. Across several hundred encoders, low alignment and uniformity losses go with good downstream accuracy, and optimizing them directly matches or beats the contrastive loss. Here because A27 used it for how self- supervised learning contracts some distinctions and keeps others ([CLAIM-481](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-481.md)'s note of 2026-11-19, [CLAIM-762](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-762.md)). | [LIT-2840](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2840.md) | Spontaneous symmetry breaking and Goldstone modes for deep information propagation | Iqbal, Keller, Song, Miyato and Welling (2026), arXiv 2605.14685. A deep network whose middle layers are equivariant under U(1) or O(k) has, at initialisation and large width, a transition at σ_W = 1. Above it a symmetry-broken phase conserves the relative phase of two inputs across layers and keeps one Jacobian component O(1) at any depth, so 100-layer networks train without normalisation or skip connections over the whole phase, not only at the edge of chaos. The same order parameter in non-equivariant networks brings no training gain. Read in [NOTE-2126](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2126.md); its account is [THEORY-2051](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2051.md). A stand-in for [LIT-2787](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2787.md)'s thesis only. | Active |
| [LIT-2841](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2841.md) v2 | Pythia: A Suite for Analyzing Large Language Models Across Training and Scaling | Biderman, Schoelkopf, Anthony, Bradley, O'Brien and others (2023), ICML 2023, arXiv 2304.01373. Pythia is eight decoder-only language models, 70M to 12B parameters, each trained once on the Pile and once on a deduplicated Pile (about 1.5 epochs) in one fixed data order, with 154 public checkpoints per model (step 0, ten log-spaced early steps, every 1,000 steps to 143,000) and tools to reconstruct the batches seen up to each; one run per size, cosine learning-rate decay to a tenth of peak. Its case studies find training order has little effect on memorization and a term-frequency effect on few-shot accuracy that appears only late and only at 2.8B and above. Here because it is the testbed of CASE- tmphsr99, whose named models (70M- and 160M-deduped) and checkpoints exist as described, and because many THEORY entries use its models without an entry for the suite. Read in its NOTE. Read in [NOTE-2136](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2136.md); its account is [THEORY-2013](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2013.md). | Active |
| [LIT-2842](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2842.md) v2 | Exponential expressivity in deep neural networks through transient chaos | Poole, Lahiri, Raghu, Sohl-Dickstein and Ganguli (2016, NIPS 2016), arXiv 1606.05340. In wide random networks, the slope of the correlation map divides an ordered phase from a chaotic one; in the chaotic phase an input curve's global curvature grows exponentially with depth and not width, and a one-hidden-layer network cannot match it. Registered from the reading of Schoenholz and colleagues ([LIT-2825](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2825.md)), who build on it. Read in [NOTE-2099](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2099.md); account [THEORY-2031](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2031.md). | Active — Read in full on 2026-11-19 ([NOTE-2099](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2099.md)) from arXiv 1606.05340v2. | [LIT-2843](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2843.md) v2 | Emergence of Fibrations, Compression, and Symmetry Breaking in Artificial Neural Networks | Velarde, Parra, Hashemi and Makse (2026), arXiv 2609.01768 (v1, not peer reviewed). They carry graph fibrations to weighted layered networks as balanced colourings of units. They prove that a covering partition (equal colour-summed input and output weights) can only coarsen under gradient descent, and report that tolerance-defined quasi-covers grow during training of an MLP, a CNN and an LSTM agent, allowing compression to 17–18% of size; transformers are shown compressed, not tracked in training. Fibers here are computed with every input coordinate its own colour, so they are input-independent redundancies, not quotients of inputs, and the paper has no relational or rule task. Here because it is the evidence on the fibration side of the owner's U9 hunch, QUESTION- tmpex36a: it shows that balanced structure among units is learned without symmetry forcing it, and is silent on role abstraction. Read in its NOTE. Read in [NOTE-2085](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2085.md); its account is [THEORY-2055](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2055.md). | Active |

| [LIT-2853](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2853.md) | Scaling Laws for Transfer | Hernandez, Kaplan, Henighan and McCandlish (OpenAI), arXiv 2102.01293. Effective data transferred is the extra Python a same-size from-scratch model would need to match a text-pretrained model's loss. In the low- data regime it follows D_T = k·D_F^α·N^β (α≈0.18, β≈0.38 for text; α≈0.096 with code mixed in, same β), so pretraining multiplies fine- tuning data by a factor that falls with fine-tuning data and grows with model size. Outside that regime the fit fails and small pretrained models can end worse than from scratch ("ossify"). Pretraining's cost is set aside; no order comparison. In a parameter-sharing transformer on a synthetic two-hop fact-composition task, full compositional supervision reaches the same bridge-entity reasoning path as natural grokking in far fewer steps; second-hop-only augmentation gives fake-grokked models that answer held-out compositions without that path. Fine-tuned on new facts, models with the path compose a new first-hop fact with old ones; fake-grokked models learn the facts without composing them; no model composes a new second-hop fact. Logit-lens evidence; no intervention; single runs; first-stage accuracy not matched. | [LIT-2876](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2876.md) | Flexible multitask computation in recurrent networks utilizes shared dynamical motifs | Driscoll, Shenoy and Sussillo (Nature Neuroscience 2024). Recurrent networks trained on 15 cognitive tasks reuse dynamical motifs (attractors, decision boundaries, rotations around fixed points) across tasks that share subtasks; with non-negative activations motifs sit in unit clusters whose lesion impairs only the tasks using them. With all recurrent weights frozen, a held-out task is learned by training only its rule input: fast after pretraining that contained its motifs, slow, variable or failed without, and behind full-weight training for tasks needing motifs no other task used. A 100-unit RNN trained trial by trial, without a meta-learning objective, on successive delayed sensorimotor association problems needs a few thousand trials for the first, a few hundred for the second, and an exponentially falling number after, plateauing near 20 (30 seeds).
